Nardev Singh Kanwar (born 24 August 1979) is an Indian politician serving as the chairman of the Himachal Pradesh Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (HPBOCWWB). He assumed office in March 2024 and is the ninth person to hold the post.
Early life and education
Kanwar was born in Luthan village in Jawalamukhi, Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh. He completed his postgraduate education at Himachal Pradesh University in Shimla. He lives in Jawalamukhi with his family and has one son.
Career
Appointment as Chairman
Kanwar was appointed chairman of the HPBOCWWB on 15 March 2024. The board implements welfare schemes for registered construction workers across Himachal Pradesh, including benefits related to education, healthcare, pensions and maternity assistance.
In his early months in office he met officials of the Labour and Employment Department to review ongoing schemes and pending claims.
Policy decisions and administrative actions
In January 2025, Kanwar welcomed the state government’s decision to shift the board’s head office from Shimla to Hamirpur, saying the change would improve accessibility for workers and administrative efficiency.
He also ordered inquiries into reported irregularities in earlier worker registrations and requested reports from district labour officers.
Awareness and outreach programmes
Under Kanwar’s leadership the board organised awareness camps to inform workers about registration and scheme benefits. Regional reporting and official notices describe multiple camps and outreach events across several districts; these activities were intended to increase registrations and inform workers about entitlements.
Digital initiatives
The HPBOCWWB portal provides online services for worker registration and access to scheme information.
In the 51st board meeting in September 2025, chaired by Kanwar, the board approved steps to expand e-KYC verification, upgrade claim-processing systems and integrate worker data with the national e-Shram portal.
Welfare disbursements
Official statements from the state government reported disbursements to registered beneficiaries administered through the board; for example, more than ₹32 crore was reported as disbursed to eligible workers under various schemes in 2024.
Board decisions and new initiatives
At the 51st board meeting the board approved, among other decisions, recruitment of Shramik Mitra posts on an outsourced basis and establishment of sub-offices and district-level outreach points to assist workers and improve service delivery.
In November 2025 the board reported opening a sub-office intended to serve workers in parts of Mandi district.
Kanwar has also participated in state-level programmes related to elderly welfare and disaster-relief contributions where the board was represented.
Official tours
According to HPBOCWWB notifications, Kanwar has undertaken official tours to districts as part of scheme reviews and outreach activities.
